sources.title: Lithuanian Universal Encyclopedia: Brushed Pottery culture
sources.note: Scholarly Lithuanian reference for archaeological scope, three long phases, settlements, buildings, economy, metallurgy, sparse burials, and chronology.

sources.title: Lithuanian Universal Encyclopedia: archaeological culture
sources.note: Reference definition of an archaeological culture as a recurring complex of finds, structures, and practices rather than a recovered self-name.

sources.title: Lithuanian Institute of History: The Stroked Pottery Culture
sources.note: Academic synthesis of chronology, open and fortified settlements, buildings, hearths, pottery, materials, food economy, and later transformation.

sources.title: Lietuvos archeologija: Skudeniai settlement structure and economy
sources.note: Peer-reviewed excavation, AMS chronology, buildings, pottery technology, crops, animals, metallurgy, activity zones, maintenance, and interpretation limits.

sources.title: Lithuanian archaeological investigations: Skudeniai unenclosed settlement
sources.note: Institutional record of the rescue excavation, postholes, finds, crops, livestock, wet hollow, fences, and brief occupation.

sources.title: Lietuvos archeologija: Pottery from Narkunai
sources.note: Peer-reviewed classification, 14,879 sherds, chronology, building abandonment, hearths, spatial patterning, and metallurgical activity areas.

sources.title: New Perspectives on the Bronze Age: Narkunai potters and metalworkers
sources.note: Academic instrumental study distinguishing household and technical ceramics, crucibles, moulds, itinerant craft, and unresolved social models.

sources.title: Archaeologia Lituana: Bronze Age bone artefacts from fortified settlements
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of bone and antler raw material, waste, manufacturing sequences, imitated forms, and possible social distinctions.

sources.title: Lithuanian Archaeological Society: Narkunai hillforts
sources.note: Institutional site account of post-built houses, stone hearths, woven timber barrier, livestock, and bronze-production remains.

sources.title: Lituanistika: Reskutenai hillfort
sources.note: Excavation record of late stroked pottery, semi-subterranean buildings, clay coating, outdoor stone hearth, spindle whorl, weights, and fourth-to-fifth-century dating.

sources.title: Lituanistika: Vilunai unenclosed settlement II
sources.note: Excavation record for lakeshore placement, pits, pottery, charcoal, burnt stone, flint reuse, disturbance, and first-to-third-century chronology.

sources.title: Lietuvos archeologija: Neris valley Iron Age settlements
sources.note: Peer-reviewed landscape survey of settlement networks, hillfort functions, chronology, site sizes, environment, and relations to later burial grounds.

sources.title: Archaeologia Lituana: the end of Brushed Pottery culture in the Neris basin
sources.note: Peer-reviewed reassessment of Kernave layers, fire and destruction evidence, dating finds, and competing internal-development or migration explanations.

sources.title: Archaeologia Lituana: Juodoniai hillfort settlement
sources.note: Peer-reviewed reanalysis rejecting simple continuous-development stories and stressing stratigraphy, activity zones, gaps, and changing research methods.

sources.title: Lietuvos archeologija: dwelling and burial artefacts
sources.note: Peer-reviewed comparison of settlement and burial finds, costume, production, exchange, Roman imports, and the mystery of Brushed Pottery burial customs.

sources.title: Archaeologia Lituana: technology of Iron Age pottery in Lithuania
sources.note: Peer-reviewed technological study of clay recipes, forming, surface treatment, firing, regional variation, and late brushed pottery.

sources.title: Interdisciplinaria Archaeologica: hilltop settlement geochemistry
sources.note: Peer-reviewed soil chemistry study showing anthropogenic signals, disturbance, uncertain feature functions, and limits of artefact-only interpretation.

sources.title: Oxford Journal of Archaeology: Lake Luokesas pile settlements
sources.note: Interdisciplinary wetland excavation of two eastern Lithuanian pile settlements dated roughly 800 to 400 BCE, with construction and preservation evidence.

sources.title: Archaeologia Lituana: Eastern and Western Lithuania watershed
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis linking the culture end to late second or early third century change while rejecting a single simple successor narrative.

sources.title: Archaeologia Lituana: trends in Lithuanian hillfort research
sources.note: Research history explaining excavation priorities, evidence imbalance, major Brushed Pottery hillfort projects, and unpublished or method-limited records.

sources.title: UNESCO: Kernave Archaeological Site
sources.note: Official heritage record for the long-lived cultural landscape, changing settlements, fortifications, and preservation responsibilities.

sources.title: Lituanistika: Kernave archaeological site and world heritage
sources.note: Academic heritage synthesis of deep occupation, Brushed Pottery settlements and burial evidence, later fortifications, and long landscape history.

sources.title: Lithuanian Archaeological Society: first lake dwellers of Lithuania
sources.note: Institutional research report on wetland settlement methods, wooden piles, organic preservation, chronology, and limits of wider comparison.

sources.title: Heritage: Zooarchaeology of Lithuanian fortified settlements
sources.note: Peer-reviewed animal-bone study of livestock, hunting, fish, mussels, tool raw material, sampling, preservation, and local economic variation.

sources.title: Archaeologia Baltica: Roman Iron Age farming practices in Lithuania
sources.note: Peer-reviewed integrated archaeobotanical, environmental, and isotope research on crop diversity, field conditions, preservation, varied management, and interpretation limits from 1 to 400 CE.

sources.title: Historic England: Human osteoarchaeology
sources.note: Official specialist guidance on what skeletal evidence can and cannot reveal about health, diet, mortality, injury, and care.

sources.title: Historic England: Wetland Heritage
sources.note: Official guidance on waterlogged preservation of wood, textiles, plants, leather, settlement evidence, and environmental threats.

sources.title: Lietuvos archeologija: Eastern Baltic burial pottery analysis
sources.note: Peer-reviewed contextual, macroscopic, and microscopic study demonstrating technological choices and limits of cultural inference from pottery.

sources.title: Lituanistika: prehistory of Upyte land
sources.note: Regional archaeological synthesis of sparse Brushed Pottery sites, stone axes, river placement, and later burial traditions.

sources.title: Lituanistika: archaeology of the Kriaunos-Obeliai area
sources.note: Regional research history and mapped comparison of eight Brushed Pottery monuments around lakes, rivers, and hillforts.

sources.title: Lituanistika: investigations at Azutakis settlement
sources.note: Excavation report on mixed-period deposits, animal bone and horn, pottery, aquiferous beds, and the need to separate occupation horizons.

sources.title: Archaeologia Lituana: fortified settlements and changing interpretations
sources.note: Peer-reviewed eastern Baltic research history separating settlement evidence, chronology, migration hypotheses, language proposals, material variation, and changing ethnic interpretations.

sources.title: Archaeologia Baltica: economy and society in Bronze Age Lithuania
sources.note: Peer-reviewed comparison of inland and coastal economies, environment, production, livestock, exchange, and cautious social interpretation.

sources.title: Lietuvos archeologija: bronze casting and communication
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis of moulds, local casting in foreign styles, exchange networks, itinerant specialists, and southeastern Baltic communication.
